power: Configure power management for block devices Add udev rule that runs a script to configure APM for block devices when supported, and the standby timeout otherwise. APM level 254 (max performance) is used when running on AC, and level 1 (lowest power) when on battery. The standby timeout is 2h on AC and 5s on battery. For SanDisk SSDs power management is not configured since the implementation is too aggressive (b/35524329). BUG=chromium:741938, chromium:214886 TEST=butterfly (w/ HDD) unplug AC # wait 30s hdparm -B /dev/sda => APM_level = 1 plug AC # wait 5s hdparm -B /dev/sda => APM_level = 254 peppy (KINGSTON SNS4151) unplug AC # wait 30s hdparm -B /dev/sda => APM_level = 1 plug AC # wait 5s hdparm -B /dev/sda => APM_level = 254 falco (LITEONIT LSS-16, APM not supported) hdparm -B /dev/sda => APM_level = not supported unplug AC # wait 30s dd if=/dev/sda of=/dev/null bs=1M skip=$(expr ${RANDOM} % 10000) \ count=1 2> /dev/null && sleep 6 && hdparm -C /dev/sda => drive state is: standby (most of the times) repeat 10x plug AC # wait 5s dd if=/dev/sda of=/dev/null bs=1M skip=$(expr ${RANDOM} % 10000) \ count=1 2> /dev/null && sleep 6 && hdparm -C /dev/sda => drive state is: active/idle repeat 10x wolf (SanDisk SSD i110) unplug AC # wait 30s hdparm -B /dev/sda => APM_level = off dd if=/dev/sda of=/dev/null bs=1M skip=$(expr ${RANDOM} % 10000) \ count=1 2> /dev/null && sleep 6 && hdparm -C /dev/sda => drive state is: standby (most of the times) repeat 10x plug AC # wait 5s hdparm -B /dev/sda => APM_level = off dd if=/dev/sda of=/dev/null bs=1M skip=$(expr ${RANDOM} % 10000) \ count=1 2> /dev/null && sleep 6 && hdparm -C /dev/sda => drive state is: active/idle repeat 10x CQ-DEPEND=CL:915302 Change-Id: Iaa3939f12640116ed4d5c06a25c8c0ee0a47eeae Signed-off-by: Matthias Kaehlcke <mka@chromium.org> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/914537 Tested-by: Dan Erat <derat@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Dan Erat <derat@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Mike Frysinger <vapier@chromium.org>

BACKPORT: drm/edid: Add DMT modes with ID > 0x50 commit bfcd74d2aeda25a78f7cc92f80650218b1bce0ca Author: Ville Syrjl <ville.syrjala@linux.intel.com> Date: Thu Apr 2 17:02:11 2015 +0300 drm/edid: Add DMT modes with ID > 0x50 DMT Version 1.0, Rev. 13 lists a bunch of new modes we don't currently have in our dmt mode table. So add them. The order may look a bit weird since it's not sorted based on the DMT ID, but this is the order they appear in the standard. I suppose they are ordered by the resolution, pixel clock, or some such factor. I decided that it's perhaps best to keep the same order as the spec. paygen: Run inside chroot Previously chromite was dependent on update_payload script for verifying update payloads. Also it was using files in au-generator.zip for payload generation and checking. However, this is not needed anymore because we always generate payloads using the latest code. Now we can just use the tools in the SDK itself for generating and verifying update. This CL starts generating and verify payloads inside the chroot. However it does not remove au-generator.zip yet. UPSTREAM: iommu/arm-smmu: Enable bypass transaction caching for ARM SMMU 500 The ARM SMMU identity mapping performance was poor compared with the DMA mode. It was found that enable caching would restore the performance back to normal. The S2CRB_TLBEN bit in the ACR register would allow for caching of the stream to context register bypass transaction information. Reviewed-by: Robin Murphy <robin.murphy@arm.com> Signed-off-by: Feng Kan <fkan@apm.com> Signed-off-by: Will Deacon <will.deacon@arm.com> (cherry picked from commit 74f55d34414c866dbf3a69e28a2f963abe61ca58) BUG=chromium:795946 TEST=Build and boot Change-Id: I074a9d887421e93cf8f97e318e537355a8b9d56e Signed-off-by: Vivek Gautam <vivek.gautam@codeaurora.org> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/914662 Reviewed-by: Tomasz Figa <tfiga@chromium.org>
